question_text: What are the requirements for incoming freshmen applying to USTP?
answer_content: You must pass the admission test and have good moral character. Submit a completed Application Form, a photocopy of your Form 138/Grade 12 report card signed by your class adviser (first to third quarter grades, or first to second quarter under the August to May calendar), proof of good moral character, a photocopy of your school ID, 2 identical 2x2 ID photos with a white background (no selfies), and an active email address.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 1, Sec. 1, pp. 6-7

question_text: How do I apply to USTP as a transferee?
answer_content: You must take the admission test, get approval from the Dean concerned before taking it, pass the screening, and fit within the enrollment quota. Submit a completed Application Form, your original Transcript of Records and Honorable Dismissal, an evaluation slip from the Chair and Dean of your chosen program, 2 identical 2x2 ID photos, an active email address, and proof of good moral character.
document_office: Admissions and Scholarships Office; Dean concerned
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 1, Sec. 1, pp. 7-8

question_text: Can I transfer to USTP during the mid-year term?
answer_content: No. Transferees are not admitted during the mid-year term. Freshmen and transferees should apply before regular semester classes start.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 1, Sec. 2, p. 11

question_text: What do foreign or international students need to apply?
answer_content: To take the admission test, submit complete and valid credentials from your previous school, a completed Application Form, a photocopy of your school ID, 2 identical 2x2 ID photos, and an active email address. After passing, you must submit the documents required under Executive Order No. 285, s. 2000 so the University can issue your Notice of Admission or Acceptance. These include your Personal History Statement, affidavit of support, authenticated scholastic records, and passport data page.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 1, Sec. 1, pp. 8-10

question_text: Is there special admission for Indigenous Peoples, displaced persons, or students from disadvantaged sectors?
answer_content: Yes, through the Affirmative Action Program. You need a certification from the regional office of the NCIP, NCFRMI, or DSWD. Applicants whose scores are 5 points below a program's cut-off shall be admitted on a first-come, first-served basis. These slots are capped at 5% of the program's total slots.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs (Affirmative Action Program Coordinator)
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 1, Sec. 3, p. 11; Title Six, Ch. 12, pp. 113-115

question_text: What is ASpecTS?
answer_content: ASpecTS (Admission for Special Talents and Skills) is for applicants who are talented in sports, arts, or technical skills but did not reach the cut-off score. Requirements are certificates of awards, training, or participation; 2 recommendation letters; a certificate of good moral character; and a letter of intent. Each category has at most 100 slots per campus each school year. Grantees who did not reach the cut-off apply to non-board programs.
document_office: Director of Sports, Director of Arts and Culture, or College Dean (technical skills); Admissions and Scholarships Office
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Six, Ch. 13, pp. 115-119

question_text: Can I change my admission test schedule?
answer_content: Yes. All applicants are given one chance to reschedule the exam. Click the Request to Reschedule link button in your PRISMS account, or contact the admission staff by text, call, or email.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, FAQ 4. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics).

question_text: I chose the home-based exam but could not connect. Can I switch to onsite?
answer_content: Yes. Home-based takers need a very strong and stable internet connection and two internet-connected gadgets (a laptop or computer for the exam and a phone for Webex). If you do not have these, or your signal stays weak, inform the admission office for a reschedule or choose onsite.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, FAQ 5. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics). Guidelines for Home Based Examination, p. 1. Date: Not stated.

question_text: Can I switch from onsite to home-based?
answer_content: The sources do not explain how to switch in this direction. They only say home-based is for residents far from the campus or with travel restrictions, and onsite is for residents near the campus.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, Step 4. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics).

question_text: I got disconnected during my home-based exam. What should I do?
answer_content: If you lose your connection during the exam, you will be removed from Webex monitoring and advised to contact the admission office at 856-1738 local 125, Mondays to Fridays, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. If your connection is unstable, you will be advised to reschedule only once. If your camera is off for one minute and adjusting does not help, your exam can be terminated or considered void.
source: Guidelines for Home Based Examination, pp. 2-3. Date: Not stated.

question_text: I missed my admission test. Can I still take it?
answer_content: Yes. All applicants are given one chance to reschedule. Use the Request to Reschedule link button in your PRISMS account, or contact the admission staff by text, call, or email.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, FAQ 4. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics).

question_text: What happens if I am late for my home-based exam?
answer_content: Late examinees are not admitted and are advised to reschedule. The Webex meeting locks at 8:45 AM for a 9:00 AM exam and at 1:45 PM for a 2:00 PM exam.
source: Guidelines for Home Based Examination, p. 2. Date: Not stated.

question_text: Why can't I upload my document in the application portal?
answer_content: Check the file first. The portal accepts only JPEG, PNG, and PDF files, up to 1 MB per upload. The applicant photo must be JPG or PNG. If the staff asked you for follow-up documents, upload them within the given period, because uploading is not possible after it ends.
source: Online Admission Portal (PRISMS), Upload section. Date: Not stated. USTP Admission FAQ, FAQ 2. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics).

question_text: How do I change the contact number or email on my application?
answer_content: The sources do not give steps for this. Your registered email is how USTP sends instructions and exam details, so contact the admission staff right away if it is wrong: 0936 037 9533, (088) 856-1738 local 125, or admissionunit.asocdo@ustp.edu.ph.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, Step 1, FAQ 2, and Contact Info. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics).

question_text: Can I change the course I applied for?
answer_content: A student who wants to change programs during registration may do so if their cut-off score matches the required cut-off score of the desired program.
source: USTP Student Handbook, 2023 Edition, Title Two, Ch. 17, Art. 1, p. 58. Date: 2023.

question_text: I passed but did not receive my enrollment email. What should I do?
answer_content: Check your spam folder. If it is not there, contact the Admission and Scholarship Office, because your email could be invalid. The email should contain your student number, username, temporary password, and a verification link.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, FAQ 6. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics). Enrollment Flow, Step 1. Date: Not stated.

question_text: How will I know if I passed the admission test?
answer_content: Wait for the result of qualifiers to be posted on the official website, or for an email saying you passed. The CDO admission page also links to Admission Examination Results (All Batches).
source: USTP Admission FAQ, Step 8. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics). Admission and Scholarship Office page (CDO), Testing links. Date: Not stated.

question_text: What is the passing score for the admission test?
answer_content: The FAQ says USTP uses a ranking system with a 40% rejection rate, so only the top 60% of test takers qualify for admission.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, FAQ 8. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics).

question_text: What documents do I need to apply?
answer_content: Prepare scanned copies of your report card or grades (Grade 12 report card or Certificate of Grades for college freshmen; Transcript of Records for transferees), an ID (Grade 12 school ID or Certificate of Registration for college freshmen; previous school ID or Certificate of Registration for transferees), a 2x2 photo with a white background, and a PSA-authenticated birth certificate. If married, merge your birth certificate and marriage certificate into one PDF.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, Step 2. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics).

question_text: The semester is not finished, so I can't submit my report card yet. What can I do?
answer_content: You may submit a certificate of available grades signed by your school principal or class adviser. For other lacking requirements, except the TOR, you may upload a completely filled-out promissory note and send it to admissionunit.asocdo@ustp.edu.ph.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, FAQ 3. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics). Admission and Scholarship Office page (CDO), Admission Promissory Note. Date: Not stated.

question_text: When can incoming freshmen apply?
answer_content: For the 1st semester of AY 2027-2028, admission applications for incoming freshmen run from November 9, 2026 to April 30, 2027. Apply through the online admission portal.
source: Academic Calendar AY 2026-2027, PDF p. 3. Date: 2026 (noted by CHED on May 12, 2026). Online Admission Portal (PRISMS), Portal. Date: Not stated.

question_text: I did not receive my exam permit or exam schedule. Why?
answer_content: For the admission test, the accepted-application email includes your exam permit, testing schedule, and test instructions. The two likely causes are incomplete or invalid documents, or an incorrect email address. If no exam details were provided, contact the admission staff right away: 0936 037 9533, (088) 856-1738 local 125, or admissionunit.asocdo@ustp.edu.ph.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, Step 6 and FAQ 2. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics).

question_text: How much is the admission exam?
answer_content: The FAQ says it is free for incoming college and transferee students. Second coursers and Earning Units (COT) pay Php 450, and Masters and PhD applicants pay Php 500, before the exam.
source: USTP Admission FAQ, FAQ 7. Date: 2021 (shown on the FAQ graphics).

question_text: What do I submit when I enroll as a freshman?
answer_content: Submit your original Form 138 (report card), original Certificate of Good Moral Character, original PSA-authenticated birth certificate, and one 2x2 ID photo. Married female students also submit an original PSA-authenticated marriage contract. All new students must also submit a medical certificate with a chest x-ray result that is not older than 6 months.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 2, Secs. 1-2, pp. 12-13; Title Six, Ch. 4, p. 109

question_text: What do I submit when I enroll as a transferee?
answer_content: Submit your Certificate of Transfer Credentials, Transcript of Records marked "For Evaluation Purposes Only," average grade requirement (GWA/GPA), and Certificate of Good Moral Character. Married female transferees also submit an original marriage contract. All new students must also submit a medical certificate with a chest x-ray result that is not older than 6 months.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 2, Secs. 1 and 3, pp. 12-13; Title Six, Ch. 4, p. 109

question_text: Can the subjects I took at my old school be credited?
answer_content: Possibly. Apply for accreditation during the enrollment period. The department chairperson decides and the Dean approves. Credited subjects cannot exceed 30% of the curriculum's total units, and validation should be done within 3 semesters from admission. Subjects should have the same title and units, or the Chair may compare syllabi if titles differ. Subjects taken within the last 5 years may be credited if they meet the conditions for your previous school's type. Use form RF 20 in duplicate and attach your Transcript of Records. Subjects are officially accredited only once your previous school sends USTP the official TOR marked Granted Transfer Credential.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 2, Sec. 3, pp. 13-15. Also: Helpdesk FAQ 34 (RF 20 form)

question_text: I stopped studying. How do I come back to USTP?
answer_content: If you withdrew, took a Leave of Absence, or went AWOL for one semester or more, you re-enroll as a returnee. You will have a re-entry interview with a guidance counselor, department chair, or college dean. Your return depends on available slots and the retention and residency policies in force at that time. Fill out the Re-Admission Form (FM-USTP-RGTR-05) with your details, the school year you last attended, and your reason for stopping. It is approved by the Program Dean, Academic Head or Campus Director and noted by the University Registrar.
document_office: Guidance Services Unit; Department Chair; College Dean
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 2, Sec. 4, p. 15; Ch. 5, Art. 4, p. 25. Also: Helpdesk FAQ 39 (Re-Admission Form, effective 10.01.21)

question_text: When can I add, change, or drop a subject?
answer_content: Within the first week of classes in a regular semester, if new sections open, a subject is dissolved, a schedule change is approved, or your schedules conflict. All cases need approval from the Dean or Academic Head. During the mid-year term, this is allowed only within the enrollment period.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 3, pp. 19-20

question_text: Can I still drop a subject after the add/drop period?
answer_content: Possibly, for meritorious reasons such as a work schedule conflict, health reasons, or a class dissolved late. The Dean or Academic Head must evaluate and approve it. Your absences must not exceed 17% of the subject's total contact hours, and you must officially drop it before the Midterm examination. Otherwise, the "Dropped due to Absence" policy applies.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 3, p. 20

question_text: Can I enroll in two degree programs at the same time?
answer_content: As a general rule, no. A regular student may enroll in a non-degree program if they had a GPA of 1.5 with no grade lower than 2.5 in the preceding term, consulted the concerned chairman about slots, stay within the maximum load, and have no schedule conflict.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 4, pp. 20-21

question_text: What is the most units I can take in a semester?
answer_content: With an approved overload, your total load cannot exceed 30 units. Graduating students may carry an additional 6 units, unless they were scholastically delinquent in the previous semester. In exceptional cases, a non-graduating student with a GPA of 1.5 may have an overload of up to 6 units. The Chair or Dean approves overloads.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 6, Art. 2, Sec. 2, pp. 27-28

question_text: What is the minimum number of units I can take?
answer_content: You should not carry less than 40% of the prescribed regular load. The exception is a graduating or irregular student whose only remaining subjects make up less than 40% of that semester's load.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 6, Art. 2, Sec. 1, p. 27

question_text: How many units can I take during the mid-year term?
answer_content: The normal load is 6 units. Under justifiable circumstances, the Dean may approve up to 9 units for graduating or non-graduating students.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 6, Art. 4, p. 28

question_text: Can I take a subject if I have not passed its prerequisite?
answer_content: No. You must pass the prerequisite first. If you do not, your enrollment in the subject that requires it becomes null and void.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 6, Art. 3, p. 28

question_text: How can we request a subject that is not offered this semester?
answer_content: You can request a petitioned class by filling out the request form. It needs a recommendation from the Dean and approval from the academic Vice Chancellors. At least 5 students are needed, and it depends on instructor availability and agreement to the approved payment rate.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 7, Art. 2, pp. 28-29

question_text: Can I take a subject at another USTP campus?
answer_content: Yes, without another admission test, if you are graduating or the course is not offered at your campus that semester. Present a certification from the deans or academic heads of both campuses to the host registrar. Courses taken at other campuses cannot exceed 40% of the curriculum's required courses.
document_office: Host Registrar; Deans/Academic Heads of both campuses
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 2, Sec. 7, p. 18

question_text: Can I transfer to another USTP campus in the same program?
answer_content: Yes, if you have completed two years of study and have a valid reason, as determined by the host Dean or Academic Head, such as a job opportunity or family transfer. You must meet the host program's cut-off score and requirements.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 2, Sec. 7, p. 18

question_text: Can I cross-enroll at another school?
answer_content: Graduating students may, with the Dean's or Academic Head's approval. The other school's program must be accredited at least Level II, the subject must not be offered at USTP, the limit is 9 units, and your total load cannot exceed 30 units. Non-graduating students clearing deficiencies may be allowed during the mid-year term on a case-to-case basis.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 17, Art. 2, pp. 58-59

question_text: What happens if my curriculum changes while I am studying?
answer_content: If you move to the new curriculum, your old courses are validated for equivalency. The Chair recommends and the Dean approves. If moving would not benefit you, such as when you have taken more than 75% of the old curriculum, you may stay on the old one as long as your remaining courses are still offered. If they are not, you may take equivalent courses or file a petition to open the course.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 2, Sec. 8, p. 19

question_text: When is enrollment and adding/dropping for the 2nd semester?
answer_content: For undergraduates in AY 2026-2027: enrollment is January 4-9, 2027, classes start January 5, 2027, and adding/dropping of subjects is January 11-13, 2027.
document_office: Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs
source: Academic Calendar AY 2026-2027, PDF p. 4. Date: 2026 (noted by CHED on May 12, 2026).

question_text: Can I submit some enrollment requirements late?
answer_content: A student was told that missing requirements can be passed within the same week, as long as everything is complete by then.
source: Student survey (Oct 28 to Nov 10, 2026)

question_text: How do I shift to another program?
answer_content: You must have completed one school year (two semesters) and file an application for shifting. You do not retake the admission test. The Deans of both colleges must approve it, based on requirements such as a qualifying exam, grades, accreditation of subjects, and available slots.
document_office: Deans of both colleges; Department Chair
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 2, Sec. 5, pp. 15-16; Ch. 17, Art. 1, p. 58

question_text: Can I shift to a different program at another USTP campus?
answer_content: Yes, but only after completing two years of study. Existing shifting policies apply, and board programs require the same admission cut-off score.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 2, Art. 2, Sec. 5, p. 16; Sec. 7, p. 18

question_text: Can I move from a night or weekend class program to a regular schedule?
answer_content: Yes, after completing 50% of your current night class program curriculum. All existing shifting policies then apply.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 7, Art. 8, Sec. 2, pp. 30-31

question_text: How do I apply for a Leave of Absence (LOA)?
answer_content: Get the leave of absence form from the Registrar's Office, submit the completed form to your Department Chair, and have it approved by the Dean. You may be granted up to one school year. Your LOA is not counted in your residency years.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 9, pp. 33-34

question_text: How do I withdraw from my program?
answer_content: Complete the Withdrawal Form from the Registrar's Office for approval by your dean or campus director. You may withdraw during the semester if your absences do not exceed 17% of contact hours. Beyond that, the dean may still allow it for meritorious reasons, such as financial problems or health reasons with a medical certificate.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 17, Art. 3, p. 59

question_text: When am I considered late, and does it count as an absence?
answer_content: You are tardy if you arrive past 25% of the scheduled class period, such as 30 minutes into a 1.5-hour class or 1 hour into a 3-hour class. Three instances of tardiness equal one absence.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 8, Art. 2, p. 31

question_text: How long should we wait if our instructor is late?
answer_content: Do not leave the classroom until the first third of the scheduled class time has passed.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 8, Art. 2, p. 31

question_text: How many absences will get me dropped from a subject?
answer_content: Three consecutive weeks of unexcused absences, or more than 17% of the semester's total contact hours (for example, 3 meetings for a class that meets for 3 hours a week). The instructor then gives you a mark of Dropped with Failure (D/F). Absences during the adding and dropping period are not counted.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 8, Arts. 2 and 4, pp. 31, 33

question_text: What absences can be excused?
answer_content: Absences due to illness, natural calamities, and official participation in curricular or non-curricular activities may be excused. For illness, submit a medical certificate from the University Physician, or from another physician if authenticated by the University Physician. You remain responsible for class requirements you missed.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 8, Art. 3, pp. 31-33

question_text: I will miss class for a school competition or activity. What should I do?
answer_content: As early as possible, get prior approval from the Dean or an authorized representative, then inform your instructors. If your participation is approved, you will be allowed to take special exams and make up other graded in-class work. Missing class for an activity that was not approved counts as an absence.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 8, Art. 3, Sec. 4, pp. 32-33

question_text: What time do classes start and end?
answer_content: Classes may start at 7:30 a.m. and end at 9:00 p.m. The colleges prepare class schedules based on the academic calendar.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 7, Art. 1, p. 28

question_text: Who can suspend classes?
answer_content: The President or Chancellor may suspend classes for valid reasons such as natural calamities or compromised peace and order. Class hours lost to events like typhoons and earthquakes must be made up.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 1, Art. 1, p. 5; Ch. 7, Art. 3, p. 29

question_text: How many major exams are there each semester?
answer_content: Four: Preliminary, Mid-term, Semi-final, and Final examinations.
document_office: Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs; Chancellor/Campus Director (schedule changes)
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 13, Art. 1, p. 49

question_text: I missed an exam. Can I take a special or late exam?
answer_content: Possibly, on a case-to-case basis. Requests need the Department Chair's approval. A late exam may be given within one week after the scheduled exam for valid reasons such as illness, an accident, or the death of an immediate family member, subject to the Dean's approval. You must present a medical or death certificate to be validated by the University Physician.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 13, Art. 2, pp. 49-50

question_text: How does the grading system work?
answer_content: Grades run from 1 to 5 in multiples of 0.25. 1.00 is the highest and 3.00 is the lowest passing grade. 3.25 to 3.50 is conditional, and 3.75 to 5.00 is failed. Other marks are INC (Incomplete), W (Withdrawn), and D/F (Dropped with Failure).
document_office: Instructor (gives grades); Office of the Director of Registrar (releases grades)
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 14, Art. 1, pp. 50-52

question_text: What does INC mean, and how do I complete it?
answer_content: INC is given at the final grading period if your class standing is passing but you did not take the final exam or complete other requirements. You must complete it within one school year (2 semesters and one mid-year term), or it automatically becomes 5.0. Completing it is your responsibility, and you may comply only once within that period.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 14, Art. 1, p. 51; Art. 4, pp. 53-54

question_text: What is the difference between D/F, W, and a grade of 5.0?
answer_content: W (Withdrawn) is given when you voluntarily and officially withdraw your registration. D/F (Dropped with Failure) is given when you drop a subject without the instructor's permission or exceed the allowed absences. A D/F is not equivalent to a failing grade of 5.0.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 8, Art. 4, p. 33; Ch. 14, Art. 1, p. 51

question_text: I got a conditional grade (3.25 or 3.50). What happens now?
answer_content: You may take a removal exam, given within the week after the scheduled final exam and before the grade submission deadline. If you pass, your grade becomes 3. If you fail, it becomes 5.0.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 13, Art. 3, p. 50; Ch. 14, Art. 5, p. 54

question_text: Can I retake an exam to improve a passing grade?
answer_content: No. A student with a passing grade cannot retake an exam to improve it.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 14, Art. 3, Sec. 2, p. 53

question_text: How can my grade be changed if there is a mistake?
answer_content: Grades can be changed only for exceptional cases: a computation error, a wrong entry, an omitted name or grade, or a basis for grading that differs from what was approved or announced. Submit a Change of Grade Form signed by the faculty member and Department Chair to the Dean's Office. Changes cannot be made beyond 30 working days after initial filing. If there is a dispute, you may appeal at the Dean's Office.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 14, Art. 3, pp. 52-53

question_text: Where can I see my grades?
answer_content: Faculty post grades in the University Information System (PRISM) according to the academic calendar. Only the Office of the Director of Registrar is authorized to officially release grades.
document_office: Office of the Director of Registrar
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 14, Art. 1, p. 51; Art. 2, p. 52

question_text: How is my GPA computed?
answer_content: Multiply each subject's grade by its academic units, add the results, and divide by your total academic units. NSTP is not included. For honors, PE (PATHFit) is included. An INC counts as 4.0 when computing a semester's GPA.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 18, p. 60; Art. 2, pp. 62-63

question_text: What happens if I fail subjects? (Warning, probation, and exit)
answer_content: First-year students after the first semester: failing 6 units means a warning; failing 9 units or more, or failing any subject twice, means probation. From the second semester of first year on, for students who have not finished 75% (4-year) or 80% (5-year) of their course work: failing 6 units means probation; failing 9 units or any subject twice means mandatory exit from the program; 2 successive probations, failing 12 units, or failing the same subject four times means permanent separation. PE and NSTP are not counted.
document_office: Department Chair; Dean/Satellite Campus Director; Registrar's Office
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 16, pp. 55-58

question_text: How many years do I have to finish my degree?
answer_content: The maximum residency is 7 years for a four-year program and 8 years for a five-year program. An approved LOA is not counted. If you do not finish within that period, you must take an additional 12 units (four-year) or 21 units (five-year), subject to the Dean's approval.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 15, pp. 54-55

question_text: When are the undergraduate exams this school year?
answer_content: 1st semester: Pre-Final, November 9-14, 2026; Final for graduating students, November 23-28, 2026; Final for all levels (non-graduating), December 9-19, 2026. 2nd semester: Preliminary, February 8-13, 2027; Midterm, March 15-20, 2027; Pre-Final, April 19-24, 2027; Final for graduating students, April 26-May 3, 2027; Final for non-graduating students, May 13-20, 2027.
document_office: Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs
source: Academic Calendar AY 2026-2027, PDF pp. 3-5. Date: 2026 (noted by CHED on May 12, 2026).

question_text: What scholarships does USTP offer?
answer_content: The University provides various scholarships and educational assistance or grants, provided by law, by external sponsors, and by the University. The handbook does not list them and refers students to the Scholarship Handbook.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 3, p. 21; Title Six, Ch. 1, p. 107

question_text: What must I do to keep my scholarship?
answer_content: Maintain the minimum GPA your program requires, give your sponsor a copy of your grades within 3 weeks after every semester, and complete all subject requirements within the semester so you do not get an INC.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Six, Ch. 1, Art. 1, pp. 107-108

question_text: Can I lose my scholarship?
answer_content: Yes. It can be terminated if you fail to maintain the minimum GPA, or if you are found guilty of a first academic offense or a non-academic grave offense. At the sponsor's discretion, your entitlement may be extended if the problem was beyond your control, such as a serious and prolonged illness.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Six, Ch. 1, Arts. 2-3, p. 108

question_text: I want to accept a different scholarship. What should I do?
answer_content: Formally communicate with the Scholarship Director if you decide to accept funding from another sponsor and waive your first scholarship.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 3, p. 21

question_text: Can I lose my free tuition if I take too long to graduate?
answer_content: Yes. Under RA 10931, students who do not complete their bachelor's degree within a year after their program's prescribed period are no longer eligible for Free Higher Education benefits. For shiftees, transferees, returnees, students on LOA, and irregular students, semesters already covered are subtracted from the current program's expected duration.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 4, pp. 21-23

question_text: Do I have to pay tuition at USTP CDO?
answer_content: Under RA 10931 (Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act), the government covers tuition and other school fees for qualified undergraduates at USTP.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: How and when do I apply for a scholarship?
answer_content: Calls for applications are posted on the USTP CDO Admission and Scholarship Office Facebook page. For several sponsored scholarships, apply online in PRISMS: Request module, Scholarship, Add Request, then choose the sponsor and upload your documents. Government programs like DOST-SEI and CHED have their own national application periods. Contact the ASO at (088) 856-1738 local 125.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Is there a work-study or student assistant program?
answer_content: The Career Center and Industry Relations Office (Ground Floor, Administration Building) can help with part-time job leads.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
document_office: Career Center and Industry Relations Office
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: I'm facing a financial emergency. Is there emergency help?
answer_content: Talk to the ASO or the OSA, who can refer you to outside help, such as the DSWD's Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) program. Guidance and Counseling can also support you through the stress.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
document_office: Admission and Scholarship Office; Office of Student Affairs
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Where do I submit City Scholarship requirements?
answer_content: At the Admission and Scholarship Office. City Scholars is listed as a merit scholarship on the CDO scholarship page.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
source: Student survey (Oct 28 to Nov 10, 2026)

question_text: What is TIS, and how do I know if I'm a TIS scholar?
answer_content: Students said to check the USTP scholarship Facebook page, or scan the QR code posted on the wall, and that validation details are posted on campus.
document_category: Scholarships, Free Tuition, and Financial Aid
source: Student survey (Oct 28 to Nov 10, 2026)

question_text: How do I apply for graduation?
answer_content: Apply at the start of your last semester. The Registrar posts the schedule on the university website and the Registrar's bulletin board. Get an Application for Graduation Form from the Registrar's Office, then get the recommending signatures of your instructors for that semester, your Department Chair, and your Dean. For AY 2026-2027, the application period is August 17 to October 31, 2026 (1st semester) and January 18 to April 3, 2027 (2nd semester).
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 19, Art. 2, p. 64. Also: Helpdesk FAQ 37 (Academic Calendar AY 2026-2027)

question_text: What do I need to graduate and join the commencement exercises?
answer_content: You must meet all the academic requirements in your curriculum. To join the commencement exercises, your candidacy must be confirmed by the Board of Regents upon the recommendation of the University Academic Council.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 19, Arts. 1 and 3, pp. 63-64

question_text: What GPA do I need to graduate with Latin honors?
answer_content: Summa Cum Laude: 1.0 to 1.25. Magna Cum Laude: 1.26 to 1.50. Cum Laude: 1.51 to 1.75. You must have no failing grade in your current curriculum and be enrolled in at least 85% of the regular load per semester, with exceptions for students who have no other required subjects to take. Transferees must earn 75% of the required academic units at USTP.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 18, p. 60; Art. 1, p. 61

question_text: How do I get on the Dean's List?
answer_content: You need a GPA of 1.75 or better (excluding NSTP) in the preceding semester with no failing grade, and at least 85% of the prescribed load and not less than 6 units. First Honor is 1.0 to 1.25, Second Honor is 1.26 to 1.50, and Third Honor is 1.51 to 1.75. You receive an honor certificate for each semester.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 18, Art. 2, pp. 61-62

question_text: What if I do not want to attend the graduation ceremony?
answer_content: Submit a formal letter to your Dean or their designated representative at least 10 days before the commencement exercises.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 21, Art. 1, p. 66

question_text: When do I need to get clearance, and how do I process it?
answer_content: All students must secure clearance at the end of each semester. Bring your ID to the Registrar's Office and follow its procedures. If an authorized person processes it for you, they must present photocopies of valid IDs of both of you. Transfer credentials and other official documents are issued only when you are cleared of all money and property accountabilities. Faculty evaluation is also a prerequisite for clearance. USTP uses an online system, USTP eClearance (clearance.ustp.edu.ph). The paper clearance form is signed by the Library, Assessment, your Dean and Student Affairs, and every undergraduate needs the Director of Student Affairs' signature for enrollment.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 20, Arts. 1 and 3, pp. 65-66; Ch. 22, Art. 1, pp. 66-67. Also: Helpdesk FAQ 16; Student's Clearance form FM-USTP-RGTR-04 (effective 10.01.21)

question_text: How do I get an Honorable Dismissal?
answer_content: If you are in good standing, present a written petition to the Registrar, signed by your parent or guardian, and settle all debts to the College. Bring your ID to the Registrar's Office. A student who leaves because of suspension, dropping, or expulsion due to disciplinary action is not entitled to honorable dismissal.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 20, Arts. 2-3, pp. 65-66

question_text: I lost my ID. What should I do?
answer_content: Submit an affidavit of loss to the Office of Student Affairs and request a new ID. The 2021 handbook also asks for a photocopy of your school ID and two identical 2x2 photos with a white background (no selfies). Students reported getting an ID request slip and having their photo taken at USTP CDO.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 5, Art. 2, Sec. 3, pp. 84-85; Title Six, Ch. 10, p. 111. Also: 2021 Student Handbook (ID Replacement); student survey; Villanueva fee list

question_text: I lost or damaged my diploma. Can I get a new one?
answer_content: Complete the application for a duplicate or replacement diploma, have your signature verified by a Notary Public, and give a notarized statement about the loss or damage. You must also certify that you will return the duplicate if the original is found. If lost, a duplicate is printed only after at least one year, unless the original is known to be destroyed. If damaged, return what was salvaged. The duplicate will be marked "iteratum" or "duplicate."
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Six, Ch. 11, Art. 1, pp. 111-112

question_text: How do I correct or change my name in my school records and diploma?
answer_content: For a major change that needs court action, give the registrar any of these: an NSO Security Paper (SECPA) showing your new legal name, a certified copy of the Final Decree for Change of Name, or a notarized Same Name Affidavit. For a minor spelling correction, present the corrected NSO-authenticated birth certificate. To replace a diploma, return the original and pay the applicable fee.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Six, Ch. 11, Art. 2, pp. 112-113

question_text: What does the Registrar's Office handle?
answer_content: It coordinates activities related to student registration, transfer, and graduation.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Six, Ch. 4, p. 109

question_text: PRISMS says I have liabilities. What should I do?
answer_content: Old students who see this during enrollment should go to clearance.ustp.edu.ph and settle their liabilities before they can proceed with enrollment.
source: Enrollment Flow, Step 6. Date: Not stated.

question_text: How can I contact the Registrar's Office?
answer_content: USTP Cagayan de Oro: +63 (088) 8571738, local 137.
source: USTP Contact Us page, Registrar entry. Date: Not stated. USTP Panaon Registrar Office page, Contact details. Date: Not stated.

question_text: How do I request my TOR or other credentials?
answer_content: No published step-by-step process was found. The handbook says transfer credentials and other official documents are issued only when you are cleared of all money and property accountabilities. For clearance and honorable dismissal, it says to bring your ID to the Registrar's Office.
source: USTP Student Handbook, 2023 Edition, Title Two, Ch. 20, Arts. 1 and 3, pp. 65-66. Date: 2023.

question_text: How long does it take to get a new school ID?
answer_content: Students reported about 1 month, or 2-3 weeks when IDs are in stock (watch the OSA Facebook page for an announcement). One student was told the release date was "to be announced".
source: Student survey (Oct 28 to Nov 10, 2026)

question_text: Where and when is ID validation?
answer_content: Students said ID validation is held at the gym lobby, with the schedule posted on campus.
source: Student survey (Oct 28 to Nov 10, 2026)

question_text: How much are required books?
answer_content: One student paid ₱510 for a required book. Prices depend on the course.
source: Student survey (Oct 28 to Nov 10, 2026)

question_text: How much is the PE uniform?
answer_content: Two students reported ₱700 for the shirt and pants, paid at the Cashier.
source: Student survey (Oct 28 to Nov 10, 2026)

question_text: Do I need to pay the PTA fee before I enroll?
answer_content: A student was told yes. A 2026 USTP article calls the group the Parents-Teachers-Community Association (PTCA).
source: Student survey (Oct 28 to Nov 10, 2026)

question_text: When do I need to wear my uniform?
answer_content: Wear the prescribed uniform on regular class days. The exceptions are Wednesdays, weekends, and days with scheduled PE classes, when students wearing their PE uniforms are allowed entry. Violations are light offenses: 3 hours of community service, then 6 hours, then no entry to campus for 1 to 3 days.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 5, Art. 2, Sec. 3, p. 85

question_text: What clothes are not allowed on campus?
answer_content: For those who identify as men: sleeveless shirts, torn or tattered jeans, rubber slippers, earrings, and unnatural hair colors. For those who identify as women: tube, spaghetti strap, halter, backless, or peek-a-boo blouses; torn or tattered jeans; short pants; micro miniskirts; see-through attire; plunging necklines; midriff blouses; rubber slippers; and unnatural hair colors. Students with religious dress restrictions may modify their uniform designs.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Seven, Appendix I, p. 120

question_text: Do I always have to wear my ID on campus?
answer_content: Yes, for the whole time you are on campus, using the proper sling. Violations are light offenses: 3 hours of community service, then 6 hours, then no entry to campus for 1 to 3 days.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 5, Art. 2, Sec. 3, pp. 84-85

question_text: What time is the campus curfew?
answer_content: 10:00 p.m. Staying on campus beyond that time without authorization is a light offense: 3 hours of community service, then 6 hours, then no entry to campus for 1 to 3 days.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 7, Art. 1, p. 28; Title Four, Ch. 5, Art. 2, Sec. 3, p. 84; Title Five, Ch. 2, Art. 9, p. 104

question_text: What is the penalty for cheating or plagiarism?
answer_content: Plagiarism, taking a test for someone else, or changing grades: 3-day suspension on the first offense, then expulsion. Copying, letting someone copy your answers, leaking test questions or answers, or writing a report or assignment for someone else: 1-day suspension, then 3-day suspension, then expulsion. In cases involving two students, both are penalized.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Committee on Student Discipline
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 5, Art. 1, pp. 77-79

question_text: What is the penalty for smoking, alcohol, gambling, or littering on campus?
answer_content: These are less grave offenses: a reprimand and 5 hours of community service on the first offense, a 3-day suspension on the second, and expulsion on the third. This also applies to entering campus under the influence of liquor.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 5, Art. 2, Sec. 2, pp. 81-84

question_text: Is cyberbullying punishable?
answer_content: Yes. Cyberbullying is included under verbal abuse, threats, and harassment, which are less grave offenses: a reprimand and 5 hours of community service, then a 3-day suspension, then expulsion.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 5, Art. 2, Sec. 2, pp. 81-82; Title Seven, Appendix V, p. 135

question_text: What offenses can get me expelled right away?
answer_content: Non-academic grave offenses carry expulsion on the first offense. These include bringing in or being under the influence of prohibited drugs, vandalism, sexual assault, hazing, possessing firearms or deadly weapons, theft, forgery of official documents, physical assault, unlawful access to computer data or systems, extortion, and writing defamatory statements.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Committee on Student Discipline
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 5, Art. 2, Sec. 1, pp. 79-81

question_text: Can I be selected for a drug test? What if I refuse?
answer_content: Yes. Undergraduate students may be randomly selected, and OSA will notify you of the schedule. Results are confidential and are not published. Refusing without a valid reason may result in a 3-day suspension, and refusing again results in dismissal from the University.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs (Drug Testing Coordinator); University Physician
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Seven, Appendix III, pp. 122-124

question_text: How do I file a complaint against another student?
answer_content: File a written, signed complaint addressed to the OSA Director. It must also be signed by the Prefect of Discipline or an authorized University official. Include the student's full name, your full name with your address and contact number or email, the relevant facts, and your evidence or witness testimonies. It will not be acted on after 30 days from the close of the term when the incident happened, unless the delay was beyond your control.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 4, Arts. 5-6 and 8, pp. 72-74

question_text: How do I file a complaint against a faculty or staff member?
answer_content: Fill out the complaint form at the Office of Student Affairs. Include the person's name and your reasons. The complaint is endorsed to the Campus Human Resources Unit and acted on following due process for University personnel.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Campus Human Resources Unit
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 6, pp. 85-86

question_text: What are my rights if someone files a complaint against me?
answer_content: You have the right to due process. This includes being told in writing of the accusation and evidence, answering the charges, presenting your own evidence, and having counsel. The OSA Director will ask you to answer in writing within 5 working days. After a decision, you have 5 working days to file a motion for reconsideration with the University President.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Committee on Student Discipline; University President
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Four, Ch. 4, Arts. 2, 10-11, 13, 17, pp. 72, 74-75, 77

question_text: Where do I report sexual harassment?
answer_content: File a complaint with your campus's Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CODI). If the complainant or person complained of is a CODI member, that member is disqualified or the complaint may go directly to the Civil Service Commission. Complaints must be filed within 3 years from the act. Withdrawing a complaint does not automatically dismiss it. The University may also provide counseling and referral to professional help.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Seven, Appendix IV, Parts B and G, pp. 128, 134

question_text: What are my rights as a USTP student?
answer_content: These include admission without discrimination, quality education, student welfare services, self-organization, representation in the Board of Regents through the University Student Government president, freedom of expression, academic freedom, and student publication.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Three, Chs. 1-8, pp. 67-69

question_text: What rules am I expected to follow?
answer_content: The Student Code of Conduct in the Student Handbook applies to all students, alongside Philippine law. You are expected to act honestly, respect others' rights, resolve conflicts without harming others, and practice temperance with gambling, drinking and drugs. Every student signs an acknowledgment of university policies during orientation; it is an OSA clearance requirement.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What are the penalties for non-academic offenses?
answer_content: Grave offenses that mean expulsion: prohibited drugs, serious vandalism, sexual assault, hazing, firearms or deadly weapons. Less grave offenses (verbal abuse or cyberbullying, stalking, lewd acts, alcohol, gambling, smoking, littering, using another student's ID): a reprimand and 5 hours of community service, then a 3-day suspension, then expulsion. Light offenses (staying past the 10:00 p.m. curfew, not wearing your ID, uniform or dress code violations, speeding on campus): 3 hours of community service, then 6 hours, then no entry to campus.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What happens after a complaint is filed against a student?
answer_content: Within 5 working days, the OSA Director asks the respondent for a written answer (copy to parents). The respondent answers within 5 working days. After a preliminary review and a possible dialogue, the Committee on Student Discipline investigates and, within 10 working days, sends its recommendation through the Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs and Services to the Chancellor, who decides within 3 working days. The student may ask the University President for reconsideration within 5 working days; that decision is final.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Committee on Student Discipline
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Will a disciplinary case affect my records?
answer_content: Yes. A reprimand stays in your permanent record. Students who leave because of suspension, dismissal or expulsion are not entitled to honorable dismissal, and their transcript or certification will state the disciplinary action. A grave non-academic offense can also end a scholarship and bars you from running in USG elections.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Can students hold protests or express their views?
answer_content: Yes. Students have the right to express their views responsibly, assemble peaceably, and air grievances through proper channels. Campus activities must still follow OSA rules on approval, posting and the 10:00 p.m. limit.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: How many student organizations can I join? Can a freshman be an officer?
answer_content: You can be a member of up to three organizations. A freshman may be a member but cannot be elected as an officer.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Five, Ch. 1, Art. 3, p. 90

question_text: How do we get our organization accredited?
answer_content: Submit these at the start of the school year: concept paper, list of officers and members, officers' personal data sheets with 2x2 photos, the moderator's letter of acceptance (regular faculty only), plan of activities, work and financial plan, constitution and by-laws, and a photocopy of the organization's bank passbook. Officers are also interviewed. Non-accredited organizations cannot hold events or use the University's name.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Arts and Culture Division (its own organizations)
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Five, Ch. 1, Art. 1, pp. 86-87

question_text: What do I need to run for student organization officer?
answer_content: You must be a duly registered student with two semesters of residency before the candidacy and no failing grade. Secure a Dean's certification of residency and an OSA certification that you have no disciplinary record involving a grave offense. Students on OJT or Student Teaching who will graduate during their last term of office cannot be President, Vice President, or Treasurer.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Dean; COMELEC/ELECOM
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Five, Ch. 1, Art. 4, Sec. 3, pp. 91-92; Art. 5, p. 94

question_text: How do we get posters approved on campus?
answer_content: Register the activity at OSA, where applicable, and present your announcements for approval, recording, and stamping. They must show the sponsoring group, activity, date, and venue. Post them only in designated places and remove them one day after the activity. Up to 4 posters are allowed, plus 1 canvas streamer for major activities involving the entire student body or USTP community.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Five, Ch. 2, Art. 6, pp. 97-98

question_text: When are student organization activities not allowed?
answer_content: Activities are suspended one week before preliminary, mid-term, and pre-final exams, and two weeks before final exams. Except in meritorious cases, activities inside the University must not go beyond 10:00 p.m.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Five, Ch. 2, Arts. 2 and 4, pp. 96-97

question_text: Can we stay overnight on campus for an activity?
answer_content: Only if necessary, for officers or members of organizing committees. The organization's President or Head sends a request letter, recommended by the Moderator, for approval by the Vice Chancellor. It must state the purpose, dates, full names of students, venue, and written parent or guardian consent. The moderator accompanies students who stay.
document_office: Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs and Services
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Five, Ch. 1, Art. 6, Sec. 3, p. 96; Ch. 2, Art. 9, p. 104

question_text: How do we get a fund-raising activity approved?
answer_content: Submit a project proposal, recommended by your moderator, to the OSA or Arts and Culture office at least one month before the event. All tickets must be pre-numbered and registered. Submit a financial report within two weeks after the activity, with any unsold tickets. Major fund-raising with solicitations also needs approval before you seek sponsors.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Arts and Culture office
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Five, Ch. 2, Art. 10, pp. 105-106

question_text: What do I need to join an educational tour or field trip?
answer_content: You must be officially enrolled in the subject, and submit a notarized parent's or guardian's consent and a medical certificate. You are expected to attend the briefings beforehand and submit learning journals after the trip. You are still accountable for other classes you miss.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs (consent and waiver form); Subject Instructor
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 10, pp. 34, 36-37

question_text: What kinds of student organizations are there?
answer_content: The University Student Government (USG), elected by all students, whose president sits on the Board of Regents; college-based mother organizations and councils; curricular organizations tied to a discipline; non-curricular organizations for leadership, service, sports, culture and advocacy; Arts and Culture groups under the ArCu Division; and the student publication.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Does USTP have fraternities and sororities?
answer_content: Not in the US sense. Any group that uses hazing to recruit or initiate members cannot be accredited and is banned. Hazing that causes harm or humiliation is a grave offense punishable by expulsion on the first offense, and a crime under the Anti-Hazing Act (RA 8049, as amended by RA 11053). Report hazing to the OSA immediately.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: How do we renew our organization's accreditation each year?
answer_content: Submit updated officer data sheets, an accomplishment report, an audited financial statement, reports on values training and environmental projects, the president's and moderator's reports, a general plan of activities, and an evaluation of the moderator, officers and organization.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What are the rules for USG election campaigns?
answer_content: The campaign period is one week before Election Day. Posters need a COMELEC stamp and may go only on COMELEC-designated boards, not on trees, walls or fences. Paid off-campus ads on radio, TV or newspapers are not allowed. Classroom campaigning needs prior permission from the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs and the instructor.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: How do we hold an event on campus?
answer_content: Register the activity with the OSA and get approval before announcing it. Submit two copies of documentation to the OSA one week before and one week after. End by 10:00 p.m. unless approved. No activities one week before prelim, midterm and pre-final exams, or two weeks before finals. Posters must be OSA-stamped and removed one day after the event. For large events, coordinate security, first aid and exits through the OSA Director.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Can we invite an outside speaker?
answer_content: Yes. Send a letter with the seminar title and the speaker's name to the Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs and Services, through channels, and get approval before the event. Consult your moderator on protocol, especially for officials and dignitaries.
document_office: Office of the Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs and Services
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Are there awards or scholarships for student leaders?
answer_content: Yes. The OSA holds the annual Kahamili Awards for outstanding students and organizations, and USTP offers an institutionally funded Leadership Scholarship.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Admission and Scholarship Office
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What are the requirements for OJT or internship?
answer_content: You must be enrolled in an internship subject, be at least 18 years old, pass the pre-internship requirements, submit a medical certificate based on an exam by a DOH-accredited clinic or hospital, have notarized written consent from your parent or legal guardian (no waiver allowed), sign the internship contract, and attend orientation. Forms are available on the USTP website.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 11, Art. 1, pp. 41-44

question_text: Can I take other subjects while on OJT?
answer_content: Yes, up to a maximum of 6 units.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 6, Art. 2, Sec. 2, p. 27

question_text: Who can apply for an international internship?
answer_content: You must be a Filipino citizen, currently enrolled with at least 75% of professional units completed or a 4th year or graduating student, at least 18 years old, in good academic standing, physically and mentally fit as certified by DOH-accredited clinics and hospitals, articulate in English or the host country's language, and have written consent from a parent, guardian, or spouse. Submit a letter of intent with supporting documents.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 11, Art. 2, pp. 44-45

question_text: How many members can a thesis group have, and how do we get an adviser?
answer_content: A group has 2 to 7 members and must be officially enrolled in research or thesis. Together with the Department Chair, you may choose an adviser or advisory committee based on your topic. If you cannot find one, the Chair may recommend a faculty member, subject to the Dean's approval.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 12, p. 47

question_text: What do we submit before our final thesis defense?
answer_content: Submit four copies of the complete manuscript, reviewed and endorsed by your adviser, to the department chair or dean at least one week before the scheduled defense.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Two, Ch. 12, p. 48

question_text: When is the medical and dental clinic open?
answer_content: Medical and dental services are available from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Mondays through Saturdays. The USTP-HIMS website lists Monday to Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Students can book free consultations, check-ups and medical certificates through USTP-HIMS (by Clinic EZ).
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Six, Ch. 6, p. 110. Also: Helpdesk FAQs 21-22; USTP-HIMS website

question_text: What services does the Guidance Office offer?
answer_content: The Guidance Services Unit offers information, counseling, testing, follow-up, and individual inventory services, among others.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Six, Ch. 5, pp. 109-110

question_text: Do I need an appointment to see the doctor, nurse or dentist?
answer_content: The walk-in and appointment policy is not published. Students can book a free appointment online through USTP-HIMS.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What health documents do I need when I enroll?
answer_content: All new students (freshmen and transferees) must submit a medical certificate with a chest x-ray result no older than 6 months. The clinic keeps it as your baseline health record.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: When else will I need a medical certificate?
answer_content: For educational tours and field trips (with a notarized parent or guardian consent); possibly for intramurals and strenuous activities (a certificate of physical fitness plus an OSA parent consent form); for OJT (from a DOH-accredited clinic or hospital, based on a physical and psychological exam); and to excuse absences due to illness (from the University Physician, or from an outside doctor and authenticated by the University Physician).
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: I'm stressed, anxious or going through a hard time. Where can I get help?
answer_content: Guidance and Counseling Services offers free, confidential counseling, psychological testing and follow-up. You can walk in, book an appointment, or be referred by a teacher or friend. You can also talk to a Listening Buddy, a student volunteer trained in Mental Health First Aid and active listening, who can connect you to a counselor.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Is counseling confidential?
answer_content: Yes. What you share with a counselor stays private, except when there is a risk of serious harm to you or someone else, or when the law requires disclosure.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What if I'm in crisis or it's after hours?
answer_content: If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 911 or go to the nearest hospital emergency room. On campus, alert any security guard or the clinic. You can also call the National Center for Mental Health Crisis Hotline at 1553, available 24/7.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What wellness activities can I join?
answer_content: The Sports Office runs physical wellness programs and intramurals. Guidance and Counseling and student organizations hold mental health talks, and the Medical Unit holds a drug-awareness symposium at least once a semester.
document_office: Sports Office; Guidance and Counseling Services; Medical Unit
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What is HIMS, and who can use it?
answer_content: The Healthcare Information Management System (HIMS) is an online health service USTP offers to its personnel and students for free.
source: USTP-HIMS website, Home page. Date: Not stated.

question_text: How do I create a HIMS account and log in?
answer_content: The USTP-HIMS website has a Join us link for signing up. A USTP study of the system says the USTP Admin handles account verification for new users, who then log in to request appointments.
source: USTP-HIMS website, Join us link. Date: Not stated. HIMS case study, Mindanao Journal of Science and Technology (USTP), Sec. 2.2. Date: January 12, 2025.

question_text: How do I get a teleconsultation?
answer_content: Log in to HIMS and request an appointment. Nurses assess your needs first, give advice, and forward complex cases to doctors. Doctors consult by secure video chat and can issue e-documents such as medical certificates and prescriptions. Services are for students and personnel, for free.
source: HIMS case study, Mindanao Journal of Science and Technology (USTP), Sec. 2.2. Date: January 12, 2025. USTP-HIMS website, Book an Appointment. Date: Not stated.

question_text: How do I fill out my Personal Health Record (PHR)?
answer_content: The PHR module in HIMS lets you enter, update, and securely store your medical history, and download it as a PDF. No published source gives the step-by-step instructions or required fields.
source: HIMS case study, Mindanao Journal of Science and Technology (USTP), PHR module section. Date: January 12, 2025.

question_text: What are the library hours?
answer_content: Undergraduate Library: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. at USTP CDO. Graduate Library: 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. E-library: 7:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. All are listed as open Mondays through Saturdays with no noon break. Hours extend up to 10 p.m. one week before Midterm and two weeks before Final exams.
source: Student Handbook 2023, Title Six, Ch. 3, p. 109

question_text: Can I use the gym and sports facilities?
answer_content: The campus gymnasium is the Dr. Ricardo E. Rotoras Memorial Hall. The Sports Office runs varsity teams, intramurals and physical wellness programs. For intramurals and strenuous activities, you may need a medical certificate of fitness and an OSA parent or guardian consent form.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: How do I try out for a varsity team?
answer_content: Contact the Sports Office. Varsity athletes may qualify for USTP's Athletic Scholarship.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: How do I reserve a room or venue for an org event?
answer_content: Get OSA approval for the activity first. Venues used for student events include the gymnasium, the Performing Arts Theater (Engineering Building) and the Cafeteria Function Hall.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Can I bring a car or motorcycle? Do I need a parking permit?
answer_content: All vehicles are inspected at the gate. Speeding on campus, by bicycle or motor vehicle, is a light offense.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Does USTP CDO have dorms or on-campus housing?
answer_content: USTP has not published a residence hall program for the CDO campus. Most students rent rooms in boarding houses or dormitories near campus, in areas such as Lapasan, Carmen, Cogon and Gusa.
document_office: Office of the Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs and Services
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: How do I find safe off-campus housing near campus?
answer_content: Visit the OSA first. Before you sign or pay: inspect the room in person, preferably with a parent or guardian; ask for a written agreement stating the rent, deposit, advance payment and included utilities; check the locks, fire exits, fire extinguisher and wiring; ask about house rules, curfew and visitors; and get a receipt for every payment.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What should I do when moving in or out of a boarding house?
answer_content: On move-in, photograph the room's condition and give your landlord's name and number to a parent or guardian. On move-out, give the notice your agreement requires, settle utilities, and ask for your deposit back in writing.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Can I change rooms?
answer_content: In a private boarding house, room changes are between you and your landlord.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What rules apply to me where I live?
answer_content: A private landlord sets the house rules. On campus and at any university activity, the Student Code of Conduct applies: no alcohol, prohibited drugs, gambling, smoking, weapons or pornographic materials, and no staying on campus past the 10:00 p.m. curfew without approval.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Who do I report a maintenance problem to?
answer_content: For a boarding house, report it to your landlord in writing and keep a copy. For a broken facility on campus, such as lights, comfort rooms, water or classroom fixtures, report it to the office in charge of campus facilities.
document_office: Auxiliary Management Services or General Services (to confirm)
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: I'm having a problem with my landlord or roommates. Who can help?
answer_content: Talk to Guidance and Counseling Services about roommate conflicts or stress. For safety concerns, harassment or disputes with a landlord, go to the OSA, which can advise you and refer you to your barangay or other authorities.
document_office: Guidance and Counseling Services; Office of Student Affairs
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Do I need to buy a meal plan?
answer_content: No. USTP does not offer meal plans. You pay per meal at the campus cafeteria or other food outlets.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Where can I eat on campus, and when is it open?
answer_content: The university cafeteria serves balanced, reasonably priced meals.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: I have a dietary restriction (halal, vegetarian, allergies). What are my options?
answer_content: If you have a serious food allergy, tell the clinic so it is in your health record, and talk to the OSA if you need an accommodation during university events.
document_office: Medical and Dental Services; Office of Student Affairs
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Can I book the cafeteria for an event?
answer_content: Yes. The cafeteria provides catering for seminars, parties and other occasions by advance reservation with the cafeteria management. Student organizations also need OSA approval for the activity.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Can my organization sell food on campus?
answer_content: Only with OSA clearance. Selling food or perishable items, branded products, or goods from charitable agencies counts as a fund-raising activity under OSA rules.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Where do I give feedback or complain about food or prices?
answer_content: Report food-safety concerns, such as suspected food poisoning, to the clinic right away.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Can I eat anywhere on campus?
answer_content: Throw your trash in the bins wherever you eat. Littering is a less grave offense: a reprimand and 5 hours of community service on the first offense.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: What protections do I have against discrimination?
answer_content: No student may be denied admission because of physical disability, socio-economic status, political or religious beliefs, sex, nationality or sexual orientation. Pregnant students and certified reformed former drug users may not be discriminated against. Report discrimination to the OSA, or gender-based harassment to the campus CODI.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Is there support for Indigenous Peoples and cultural groups?
answer_content: There is no separate cultural center listed for CDO. Support comes through the Affirmative Action Program under the OSA, the Grant-in-Aid for Minority and NCIP scholarships, and the Arts and Culture Division, which promotes Mindanao culture and indigenous traditions.
document_office: Office of Student Affairs; Arts and Culture Division
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Is there support for LGBTQ+ students?
answer_content: Sexual orientation is a protected ground in admission. Derogatory remarks about a person's sex or sexual orientation count as sexual harassment under USTP policy. The university runs a Gender and Development (GAD) program with a GAD Focal Point System. The Safe Spaces Act (RA 11313) also prohibits gender-based harassment in schools.
document_office: GAD Focal Point System; Office of Student Affairs
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: I have a disability. How do I request accommodations?
answer_content: Disability is never grounds for denying admission. Information about your disability is kept confidential and shared only as needed to arrange support.
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: I'm pregnant or a student-parent. Can I continue my studies?
answer_content: Yes. Pregnant students shall not be discriminated against. Talk to Guidance and Counseling Services and the clinic about support, and coordinate with your college about schedules.
document_office: Guidance and Counseling Services; Medical and Dental Services
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: Who do I talk to if I feel excluded or treated unfairly?
answer_content: Start with Guidance and Counseling Services for confidential support, or the OSA to report a concern. For gender-based or sexual harassment, file with the campus CODI. You can also reach the USG, which represents students to the administration.
document_office: Guidance and Counseling Services; Office of Student Affairs; CODI
source: Student Affairs FAQs (2021 Student Handbook and USTP pages)

question_text: I forgot my PRISMS password. How do I reset it?
answer_content: On the PRISMS login page, click the forgot password link and enter your email address to reset your password.
source: PRISMS login page, Login page. Date: Not stated.

question_text: I can't log in to PRISMS. What should I check?
answer_content: New students should first click the verification link in the USTP email, then log in with the username and temporary password from that email and change the password. The login page can also resend an activation code to your email. Account creation is currently disabled there, and the page says to contact USTP Admission about account creation concerns.
source: Enrollment Flow, Steps 1-3. Date: Not stated. PRISMS login page, Login page notice. Date: Not stated.

question_text: How do I pre-enroll in PRISMS?
answer_content: Log in, open the Enrollment tab or tile, and click Continue on your auto-filled details. In Advising, choose your class section, tick your subjects, and click Register selected. Confirm your details, then click Print Pre Assessment. A confirmation is sent to your registered email.
source: Enrollment Flow, Steps 4-11. Date: Not stated.

question_text: PRISMS says my information is incomplete. How do I fix it?
answer_content: Click the Click Here prompt, go to your Profile, open My student information, complete the required fields, and click Update.
source: Enrollment Flow, Step 5. Date: Not stated.

question_text: What is USTeP?
answer_content: USTeP is the USTP e-learning portal. It is where you find learning materials for each course, assignments, quizzes, and course evaluations. Each student logs in with their credentials.
source: USTP Virtual Week of Welcome: Academics, E-Learning Portal section. Date: 2021.

question_text: I forgot my USTeP password. How do I reset it?
answer_content: On the Forgotten Password page, submit your username or email address. If you are found in the database, an email is sent to your address with instructions on how to get access again.
source: USTeP Forgotten Password page, Password reset page. Date: Not stated.

question_text: One of my subjects is missing in USTeP. Why?
answer_content: A 2020 memo says the Digital Transformation Project (DTP) team links USTeP with PRISM so students and faculty are automatically registered to their assigned courses, and that the DTP assists with USTeP concerns. It does not give steps for fixing a missing subject.
source: OVPAA Memo 028, Guidelines for 1st Sem AY 2020-2021, Item 4. Date: AY 2020-2021.

question_text: I can't log in to USTeP. What should I do?
answer_content: Try resetting your password on the Forgotten Password page using your username or email address. No published source lists USTeP login errors or fixes.
source: USTeP Forgotten Password page, Password reset page. Date: Not stated.

question_text: I have no courses in USTeP. Why?
answer_content: A 2020 memo says the Digital Transformation Project team links USTeP with PRISM so students are automatically registered to their assigned courses, and that the team assists with USTeP concerns. It does not give steps for fixing this.
source: OVPAA Memo 028, Guidelines for 1st Sem AY 2020-2021, Item 4. Date: AY 2020-2021.

question_text: Where do I report other USTeP concerns?
answer_content: Open a ticket on the USTP Helpdesk and choose the matching help topic. A valid email address is required. Every request gets a unique ticket number that you can use to track its progress and responses online.
source: USTP Helpdesk Ticket, Home page and Open a New Ticket. Date: Footer shows 2026.
